name: Jambres
title: Egyptian magician who opposed Moses
summary: Jambres was one of the Egyptian magicians (along with Jannes) who opposed Moses and Aaron at Pharaoh's court. They tried to imitate the miracles God performed through Moses, but ultimately could not match God's power. They are mentioned by name only in the New Testament as examples of resistance against the truth.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to Moses at Pharaoh's court
keyEvents.description: Jambres and Jannes were among the Egyptian wise men and magicians whom Pharaoh summoned to imitate the signs that Moses and Aaron performed by God's power.

keyEvents.title: Imitation of the staff turning into a snake
keyEvents.description: When Aaron threw his staff before Pharaoh and it turned into a snake, the Egyptian magicians managed to do the same with their secret arts, but Aaron's staff swallowed theirs.

keyEvents.title: Imitation of the plague of blood
keyEvents.description: When Moses and Aaron struck the water in the Nile and it turned to blood, Jambres and the other magicians imitated this sign with their arts.

keyEvents.title: Imitation of the Frog Plague
keyEvents.description: The magicians were also able to bring forth frogs over Egypt, but this was the last plague they were able to imitate.

keyEvents.title: Failed Imitation of the Gnats Plague
keyEvents.description: When Moses and Aaron brought about the gnat plague, the magicians could not imitate this miracle and had to admit that it was 'the finger of God'.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as a Warning Example by Paul
keyEvents.description: The apostle Paul mentions Jannes and Jambres by name as examples of people who resisted the truth, with a corrupt mind and a failed faith, and uses them as a warning for the last days.
